#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run from your MONOREPO root (not from this Lovable repo).
# Syncs the operation-dashboard-ui-07 Lovable submodule into
# crates/op-web/ui, installs npm deps there, builds, and pokes
# rust-embed so `cargo build` picks up the new dist/.
set -euo pipefail

SOURCE_DIR="operation-dashboard-ui-07"
CRATE_UI_DIR="crates/op-web/ui"

echo "🚀 Updating embedded UI crate from $SOURCE_DIR submodule..."

if [ ! -d "$SOURCE_DIR/src" ]; then
  echo "❌ $SOURCE_DIR/src missing. Run: git submodule update --init --recursive"
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$CRATE_UI_DIR/src"

echo "📦 Syncing source tree..."
rsync -av --delete "$SOURCE_DIR/src/"    "$CRATE_UI_DIR/src/"
rsync -av --delete "$SOURCE_DIR/public/" "$CRATE_UI_DIR/public/" 2>/dev/null || true

# Config files Lovable may have updated
for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
         tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
         vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json package-lock.json; do
  [ -f "$SOURCE_DIR/$f" ] && rsync -av "$SOURCE_DIR/$f" "$CRATE_UI_DIR/$f"
done

pushd "$CRATE_UI_DIR" >/dev/null

# Ensure required libs
EXTRA=""
grep -q '"@json-render/react"' package.json || EXTRA="$EXTRA @json-render/react @json-render/core"
grep -q '"reactflow"'          package.json || EXTRA="$EXTRA reactflow"
if [ -n "$EXTRA" ]; then
  echo "📥 Installing missing deps:$EXTRA"
  npm install --save --legacy-peer-deps $EXTRA
fi

echo "📦 npm install..."
npm install --silent --legacy-peer-deps

echo "🏗  npm run build..."
npm run build

popd >/dev/null

echo "🧹 Invalidating rust-embed cache..."
touch crates/op-web/build.rs 2>/dev/null || true
touch crates/op-web/src/embedded_ui.rs 2>/dev/null || true

echo "✅ UI embedded at $CRATE_UI_DIR/dist — next 'cargo build' will pick it up."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "🚀 Syncing UI between local and Lovable repo (operation-dashboard-ui-07)..."

# Direction depends on FLAGS:
#   No flag: Pull Lovable changes into local (including generated codegen)
#   --push: Push local changes into Lovable (excluding gen/, which is Lovable-managed)

LOVABLE_DIR="${LOVABLE_DIR:-../operation-dashboard-ui-07}"
LOCAL_UI_SRC="crates/op-web/ui/src"
LOCAL_UI_PROTOS="crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto"
LOVABLE_SRC="$LOVABLE_DIR/src"
LOVABLE_PROTOS="$LOVABLE_DIR/proto"

    # Push local edits TO Lovable (hand-edited source only, not generated)

    mkdir -p "$LOVABLE_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/" "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/"
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \

        [ -f "crates/op-web/ui/$f" ] && rsync -av "crates/op-web/ui/$f" "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f"
    done
else

    echo "📥 Pulling LOVABLE changes → local source..."
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_SRC/" "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/" "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/"

        [ -f "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" ] && rsync -av "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" "crates/op-web/ui/$f"
    done
fi

echo "🏗️ Building UI (op-web serves from static dir immediately)..."
npm run build --prefix crates/op-web/ui

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    pushd "$LOVABLE_DIR" >/dev/null
    git add -A
    git commit -m "Sync from local op-web/ui source (auto)" || true
    git push origin zeroclaw

    echo "✅ Pushed to Lovable GitHub."
else

fi

content.text:
**Two approaches for generating gRPC/web types from plugin schemas:**

---

### **Option 1: Proto-driven (`.proto` files)**

**How it works:**
- Each plugin (persona, blockchain, btrfs, etc.) has a corresponding `.proto` file in `proto/`
- Lovable runs `bun run proto:gen` → protobuf-ts generates:
  - TypeScript interfaces for all messages/enums (`cognitive.ts`, `mail.ts`, etc.)
  - Typed gRPC clients (`cognitive.client.ts`, `mail.client.ts`, etc.)
- Frontend imports from `@/grpc/gen/*` instead of hand-written `@/grpc/types/*`

**Relation to gRPC/reflection:**
- **gRPC:** The `.proto` files ARE the gRPC message contracts. protobuf-ts generates TypeScript that exactly matches what the gRPC server expects
- **Reflection:** Server reflection (`op-grpc-bridge`) serves the same `.proto` definitions — they stay in sync
- **Blob sealing:** When plugins are sealed, the `FileDescriptorSet` section contains the compiled protobuf descriptors (derived from these same `.proto` files)

**Pros:** Single source of truth, automatic sync, all fields/types match server
**Cons:** Need to write `.proto` files for every domain type

---

### **Option 2: Schema-driven (JSON Schema → TS)**

**How it works:**
- Sealed blobs in `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/*.blob` contain `PluginSchema` JSON (not protobuf, but json-schema format)
- A generator reads this JSON + extracts the gRPC method shapes
- Emits TypeScript interfaces matching what the methods expect

**Relation to gRPC/reflection:**
- **gRPC:** The blob `PluginSchema` JSON describes D-Bus + MCP shapes, NOT protobuf messages. Server reflection still serves protobuf descriptors
- **Reflection:** Still works unchanged — serves protobuf descriptors
- **But:** Type generation would need to understand the mapping from `PluginSchema` JSON → the actual gRPC message types

**Pros:** Types derived from actual live schema state
**Cons:** Complex mapping (PluginSchema JSON → protobuf wire types), not directly compatible with gRPC reflection

---

**Recommendation:** Use **Option 1** (proto-driven). The domain plugins need `.proto` files anyway for gRPC compatibility. Once we add them, Lovable can regenerate everything in one pass.

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

3tched / OP-DBUS: a native, deterministic control plane for Artix Linux infrastructure (s6 supervision, NOT systemd). ~38-crate Rust workspace under `crates/`, plus a Vite/React/shadcn frontend. All source lives inside `crates/` workspace members — never a generic top-level `src/`. Other top-level dirs: `deploy/` (Artix s6 service defs + install scripts), `schemas/` (JSON schemas loaded at runtime), `docs/`. This file is the authoritative agent guidance; where any doc and the tree disagree, the tree wins.

## Build, lint, test

All cargo commands run from the repo root (the workspace root).

```bash
cargo build --workspace                 # build everything
cargo check -p <crate>                  # fast check a single crate (do this before edits)
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
cargo test -p <crate> <test_name>       # single test
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Frontend — there are **two** Vite apps; don't confuse them:

1. `crates/` (`vite_react_shadcn_ts`, source in `crates/src/`) — the primary UI dev tree; all npm commands below run here.
2. `crates/op-web/ui/` (`zeroclaw-gui-repo`) — the app **op-web actually embeds** (RustEmbed of `ui/dist/`). Its package.json has no `build` script (and build.rs's error message suggesting `npm run build` is stale); rebuild with `npx vite build` from that directory. Building `crates/` does NOT update what op-web serves.

```bash
cd crates
npm run dev / build / lint / typecheck
npm test                                # vitest run
npx vitest run src/test/<file>          # single test file
```

Build gotchas:

- `[patch.crates-io]` pins zbus to a **local checkout at `/home/jeremy/git/zbus`** — the workspace does not build without it.
- `op-web` **release** builds panic unless `crates/op-web/ui/dist/index.html` exists (RustEmbed); build that UI first (`npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui`). Dev builds compile with an empty asset set, so the panic only bites on `--release`.
- The root `op-dbus` package has no binary — real binaries live in member crates (`op-web` → `op-web-server`/`opdbus`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-projection` → `projection_server`, `op-s6-systemctl` → `s6d`, etc.).
- `op-ml` is commented out of the workspace (ort API breakage).
- Rust-first: no new Python; scripts are shell.

## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants

**D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`; reads, writes, and tool calls go through it (`PluginService.CallMethod`, or the `zbusctl` operator CLI — installed at `~/.cargo/bin/zbusctl`, not built from this repo). No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops or D-Bus watchers in plugin/service code — bootstrap scripts are the only exception. New backend capabilities are **plugins registered in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`**, never new gRPC proto service packages.

**PluginSchema is the single source of truth.** D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers all derive from the schema; validate inputs against it. Any derived value (e.g. a catalog hash) is computed in exactly one function, one place. Current layout: each plugin defines a `<name>_schema()` function in its own file under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, aggregated via `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`; a runtime JSON loader also reads `schemas/plugin/*.json` (repo root) via `schema_loader.rs`. NOTE: older docs claim all schemas live in a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — **that file does not exist**; single-file consolidation is planned work (`FACTORY-PROMPT-plugin-schema-uniformization.md`), not present reality.

**The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog in shared memory: `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` (`op_blob::catalog::DEFAULT_SHM_DIR`). A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog; register = seal, deregister = remove. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob` — never SchemaEngine (`op-projection`'s `write_schemas_to_shm` only reports the published catalog hash via `op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash()`). Consumers read SHM directly (1:1 zero-copy) — they never re-hash, never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder, `live-schema.json` monolith, and manifest are gone; docs that mention them are stale.

**Reactive, not polled.** The system does not watch, poll, or index. SHM is the authoritative present-state that components read; an arrival (e.g. an xray greeting connection) triggers action. Durability is the per-mutation immutable blockchain (`op-blockchain`) — there are no snapshot backups and **no SQL for state** (graph store is CozoDB).

**Transport & identity (zero-trust).** gRPC (tonic, TLS mandatory) over Unix domain sockets internally; containers get **no NIC or IP** — all container I/O is UDS. Identity = WireGuard pubkey → Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey) sessionid; a container's name IS its sessionid. The xray router injects identity headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`/`X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) — that header is the only gate; IP ACLs/ports are theater. SESSION bus = the WG-identity-gated plugin surface; SYSTEM bus = local agents/mirror.

**MCP gateways (settled — do not redesign).** `op-cognitive-mcp` is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (tonic-web gRPC :50052 + server reflection for tool discovery). `compact-mcp` is loopback-only for the chatbot. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.

**Host tooling.** Manage s6 services via the `s6d` CLI (from `op-s6-systemctl`), not raw `s6-svc`. OVS is driven natively over OVSDB JSON-RPC via the rovs plugins (`op-openvswitch-daemon` is deprecated — don't extend it). Containers are Incus; expose sockets via `zbusctl createsocket`, not raw incus proxy devices.

## Crate map (the ones you'll actually touch)

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `op-plugins` | Plugin registry + all state plugins + per-plugin schema functions (the schema source) |
| `op-projection` | SchemaEngine — schema registration/audit; reads the published catalog hash (blob sealing lives in `op-blob`) |
| `op-web` | Axum HTTP server, embeds the UI, `opdbus` CLI |
| `op-grpc-bridge` | tonic gRPC bridge (TLS) between D-Bus surface and external clients |
| `op-cognitive-mcp` | External MCP gateway, CozoDB memory, Qdrant semantic search |
| `op-identity` | WireGuard identity, sessionid derivation, sled/shuttle |
| `op-blockchain` | Per-mutation immutable chain (the durability layer) |
| `op-blob` / `op-state-store` | Sealed blob catalog / schema engine storage |
| `op-network` | Native OVSDB, OpenFlow, rtnetlink (no CLI subprocesses) |
| `op-s6-systemctl` | `s6d` service-management CLI |
| `op-xray-daemon` | xray router daemon (identity injection, subdomain routing) |
| `op-gemma` | Gemma inference plugin (schema-driven UI generation) |

## Identifiers (subid taxonomy — mandatory)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool carries a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) **and** a `subid`:

```
<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]
```

- Exactly seven categories, no others: `src` (authoritative source/ingress), `prj` (D-Bus projection/mirror publication), `sch` (schema/contract/vocabulary), `mut` (write path), `obs` (read/query/discovery), `evt` (emitted signal/audit event/proof), `exp` (consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC view).
- Component-type reuses OSCAL vocabulary (`software`, `service`, `network`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, …).
- `mut.*` must carry `actor_id` + `capability_id`; `evt.*` must carry `event_id`/`event_hash`.
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` (`ns`/`name`/`value`), never embedded in `remarks`; compliance mappings (`control_refs[]` etc.) live in metadata arrays, never inside the subid string.
- Subids are immutable per subject — material meaning changes get a new subject with `@vN`. All subids are registered in the canonical registry (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`); uniqueness is CI-enforced.
- Examples: `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`

## Conventions

- Rust: edition 2021, rustfmt (4-space, width 100), specific imports, `anyhow::Result` for app errors + `thiserror` for custom enums, `simd_json` preferred over `serde_json`.
- TypeScript/React: 2-space, functional components only, strict mode. Additional conventions in `.factory/rules/typescript.md` and `.factory/rules/testing.md`.
- `SIGNALS.md` (repo root): proactively append suggestions/concerns/observations there rather than letting them evaporate in chat. `WISHLIST.md` is the canonical task board — don't create new TODO docs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "🚀 Syncing UI between local and Lovable repo (operation-dashboard-ui-07)..."

# Direction depends on FLAGS:
#   No flag: Pull Lovable changes into local (including generated codegen)
#   --push: Push local changes into Lovable (excluding gen/, which is Lovable-managed)

LOVABLE_DIR="${LOVABLE_DIR:-../operation-dashboard-ui-07}"
LOCAL_UI_SRC="crates/op-web/ui/src"
LOCAL_UI_PROTOS="crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto"
LOVABLE_SRC="$LOVABLE_DIR/src"
LOVABLE_PROTOS="$LOVABLE_DIR/proto"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    # Push local edits TO Lovable (hand-edited source only, not generated)
    echo "📤 Pushing LOCAL source → Lovable repo..."
    rsync -av --delete "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/" "$LOVABLE_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOVABLE_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/" "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/"
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
             vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json; do
        [ -f "crates/op-web/ui/$f" ] && rsync -av "crates/op-web/ui/$f" "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f"
    done
else
    # Default: Pull Lovable changes INTO local (including generated codegen)
    echo "📥 Pulling LOVABLE changes → local source..."
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_SRC/" "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/" "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/"
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
             vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json; do
        [ -f "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" ] && rsync -av "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" "crates/op-web/ui/$f"
    done
fi

echo "🏗️ Building UI (op-web serves from static dir immediately)..."
npm run build --prefix crates/op-web/ui

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    pushd "$LOVABLE_DIR" >/dev/null
    git add -A
    git commit -m "Sync from local op-web/ui source (auto)" || true
    git push origin zeroclaw
    popd >/dev/null
    echo "✅ Pushed to Lovable GitHub."
else
    echo "✅ Pulled and built. Local op-web now serves updated UI."
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "🚀 Syncing UI between local and Lovable repo (operation-dashboard-ui-07)..."

# Direction depends on FLAGS:
#   No flag: Pull Lovable changes into local (including generated codegen)
#   --push: Push local changes into Lovable (excluding gen/, which is Lovable-managed)

LOVABLE_DIR="${LOVABLE_DIR:-../operation-dashboard-ui-07}"
LOCAL_UI_SRC="crates/op-web/ui/src"
LOCAL_UI_PROTOS="crates/op-web/ui/proto"
LOVABLE_SRC="$LOVABLE_DIR/src"
LOVABLE_PROTOS="$LOVABLE_DIR/proto"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    # Push local edits TO Lovable (hand-edited source only, not generated)
    echo "📤 Pushing LOCAL source → Lovable repo..."
    rsync -av --delete "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/" "$LOVABLE_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOVABLE_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/" "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/"
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
             vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json; do
        [ -f "crates/op-web/ui/$f" ] && rsync -av "crates/op-web/ui/$f" "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f"
    done
else
    # Default: Pull Lovable changes INTO local (including generated codegen)
    echo "📥 Pulling LOVABLE changes → local source..."
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_SRC/" "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/" "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/"
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
             vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json; do
        [ -f "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" ] && rsync -av "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" "crates/op-web/ui/$f"
    done
fi

echo "🏗️ Building UI (op-web serves from static dir immediately)..."
npm run build --prefix crates/op-web/ui

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    pushd "$LOVABLE_DIR" >/dev/null
    git add -A
    git commit -m "Sync from local op-web/ui source (auto)" || true
    git push origin zeroclaw
    popd >/dev/null
    echo "✅ Pushed to Lovable GitHub."
else
    echo "✅ Pulled and built. Local op-web now serves updated UI."
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "🚀 Syncing UI between local and Lovable repo (operation-dashboard-ui-07)..."

# Direction depends on FLAGS:
#   No flag: Pull Lovable changes into local (including generated codegen)
#   --push: Push local changes into Lovable (excluding gen/, which is Lovable-managed)
#   --dump-protos: Export dynamic protos from SHM blobs to Lovable before push

# Handle --dump-protos first
if [ "${DUMP_PROTOS:-}" = "1" ] || [ "${1:-}" = "--dump-protos" ]; then
    echo "📦 Exporting dynamic protos from SHM blobs..."
    if [ -x "./target/debug/dump-protos" ]; then
        ./target/debug/dump-protos operation-dashboard-ui-07/proto/ 2>&1 | grep -v "already written" || true
    else
        echo "⚠️  dump-protos not compiled - run 'cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge --bin dump-protos' first"
    fi
fi

LOVABLE_DIR="${LOVABLE_DIR:-../operation-dashboard-ui-07}"
LOCAL_UI_SRC="crates/op-web/ui/src"
LOCAL_UI_PROTOS="crates/op-web/ui/proto"
LOVABLE_SRC="$LOVABLE_DIR/src"
LOVABLE_PROTOS="$LOVABLE_DIR/proto"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    # Push local edits TO Lovable (hand-edited source only, not generated)
    echo "📤 Pushing LOCAL source → Lovable repo..."
    rsync -av --delete "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/" "$LOVABLE_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOVABLE_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/" "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/"
    # Also sync dynamic plugin protos from op-grpc-bridge target/debug
    if [ -d "crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto" ]; then
        rsync -av "crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/" "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/../" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    # Sync plugin_methods from dump-protos output (if exists)
    if [ -d "target/debug/proto/plugin_methods" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/plugin_methods"
        rsync -av "target/debug/proto/plugin_methods/" "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/plugin_methods/" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
             vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json; do
        [ -f "crates/op-web/ui/$f" ] && rsync -av "crates/op-web/ui/$f" "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f"
    done
else
    # Default: Pull Lovable changes INTO local (including generated codegen)
    echo "📥 Pulling LOVABLE changes → local source..."
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_SRC/" "$LOCAL_UI_SRC/"
    mkdir -p "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS"
    rsync -av "$LOVABLE_PROTOS/" "$LOCAL_UI_PROTOS/"
    for f in index.html components.json tailwind.config.ts postcss.config.js \
             tsconfig.json tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json \
             vite.config.ts eslint.config.js package.json; do
        [ -f "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" ] && rsync -av "$LOVABLE_DIR/$f" "crates/op-web/ui/$f"
    done
fi

echo "🏗️ Building UI (op-web serves from static dir immediately)..."
npm run build --prefix crates/op-web/ui

if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    pushd "$LOVABLE_DIR" >/dev/null
    git add -A
    git commit -m "Sync from local op-web/ui source (auto)" || true
    git push origin zeroclaw
    popd >/dev/null
    echo "✅ Pushed to Lovable GitHub."
else
    echo "✅ Pulled and built. Local op-web now serves updated UI."
fi

   • Removed concatenated originals and .bak files

   Sync protobuf files to Lovable repository so it can generate TypeScript types via `proto:gen` - each `.proto` file must have exactly one `syntax = "proto3"` + `package` declaration to be valid for `protoc-ts`.

   - Verified Lovable repo location and pushed to correct GitHub repository

7. Error Resolution
   - **Invalid proto format**: plugin_methods/*.proto had multiple `syntax="proto3"` + `package` declarations → Split into separate files with unique package names
   - **Wrong repo location**: Was syncing to subdirectory in main repo → Fixed to use separate Lovable repo path

8. Pending Tasks

<coding_guidelines>
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

3tched / OP-DBUS: a native, deterministic control plane for Artix Linux infrastructure (s6 supervision, NOT systemd). ~38-crate Rust workspace under `crates/`, plus a Vite/React/shadcn frontend. All source lives inside `crates/` workspace members — never a generic top-level `src/`. Other top-level dirs: `deploy/` (Artix s6 service defs + install scripts), `schemas/` (JSON schemas loaded at runtime), `docs/`. This file is the authoritative agent guidance; where any doc and the tree disagree, the tree wins.

## Build, lint, test

All cargo commands run from the repo root (the workspace root).

```bash
cargo build --workspace                 # build everything
cargo check -p <crate>                  # fast check a single crate (do this before edits)
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
cargo test -p <crate> <test_name>       # single test
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Frontend — there are **two** Vite apps; don't confuse them:

1. `crates/` (`vite_react_shadcn_ts`, source in `crates/src/`) — the primary UI dev tree; all npm commands below run here.
2. `crates/op-web/ui/` (`zeroclaw-gui-repo`) — the app **op-web actually embeds** (RustEmbed of `ui/dist/`). Its package.json has no `build` script (and build.rs's error message suggesting `npm run build` is stale); rebuild with `npx vite build` from that directory. Building `crates/` does NOT update what op-web serves.

```bash
cd crates
npm run dev / build / lint / typecheck
npm test                                # vitest run
npx vitest run src/test/<file>          # single test file
```

Build gotchas:

- `[patch.crates-io]` pins zbus to a **local checkout at `/home/jeremy/git/zbus`** — the workspace does not build without it.
- `op-web` **release** builds panic unless `crates/op-web/ui/dist/index.html` exists (RustEmbed); build that UI first (`npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui`). Dev builds compile with an empty asset set, so the panic only bites on `--release`.
- The root `op-dbus` package has no binary — real binaries live in member crates (`op-web` → `op-web-server`/`opdbus`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-projection` → `projection_server`, `op-s6-systemctl` → `s6d`, etc.).
- `op-ml` is commented out of the workspace (ort API breakage).
- Rust-first: no new Python; scripts are shell.

## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants

**D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`; reads, writes, and tool calls go through it (`PluginService.CallMethod`, or the `zbusctl` operator CLI — installed at `~/.cargo/bin/zbusctl`, not built from this repo). No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops or D-Bus watchers in plugin/service code — bootstrap scripts are the only exception. New backend capabilities are **plugins registered in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`**, never new gRPC proto service packages.

**PluginSchema is the single source of truth.** D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers all derive from the schema; validate inputs against it. Any derived value (e.g. a catalog hash) is computed in exactly one function, one place. Current layout: each plugin defines a `<name>_schema()` function in its own file under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, aggregated via `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`; a runtime JSON loader also reads `schemas/plugin/*.json` (repo root) via `schema_loader.rs`. NOTE: older docs claim all schemas live in a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — **that file does not exist**; single-file consolidation is planned work (`FACTORY-PROMPT-plugin-schema-uniformization.md`), not present reality.

**The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog in shared memory: `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` (`op_blob::catalog::DEFAULT_SHM_DIR`). A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog; register = seal, deregister = remove. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob` — never SchemaEngine (`op-projection`'s `write_schemas_to_shm` only reports the published catalog hash via `op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash()`). Consumers read SHM directly (1:1 zero-copy) — they never re-hash, never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder, `live-schema.json` monolith, and manifest are gone; docs that mention them are stale.

**Reactive, not polled.** The system does not watch, poll, or index. SHM is the authoritative present-state that components read; an arrival (e.g. an xray greeting connection) triggers action. Durability is the per-mutation immutable blockchain (`op-blockchain`) — there are no snapshot backups and **no SQL for state** (graph store is CozoDB).

**Transport & identity (zero-trust).** gRPC (tonic, TLS mandatory) over Unix domain sockets internally; containers get **no NIC or IP** — all container I/O is UDS. Identity = WireGuard pubkey → Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey) sessionid; a container's name IS its sessionid. The xray router injects identity headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`/`X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) — that header is the only gate; IP ACLs/ports are theater. SESSION bus = the WG-identity-gated plugin surface; SYSTEM bus = local agents/mirror.

**MCP gateways (settled — do not redesign).** `op-cognitive-mcp` is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (tonic-web gRPC :50052 + server reflection for tool discovery). `compact-mcp` is loopback-only for the chatbot. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.

**Host tooling.** Manage s6 services via the `s6d` CLI (from `op-s6-systemctl`), not raw `s6-svc`. OVS is driven natively over OVSDB JSON-RPC via the rovs plugins (`op-openvswitch-daemon` is deprecated — don't extend it). Containers are Incus; expose sockets via `zbusctl createsocket`, not raw incus proxy devices.

## Crate map (the ones you'll actually touch)

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `op-plugins` | Plugin registry + all state plugins + per-plugin schema functions (the schema source) |
| `op-projection` | SchemaEngine — schema registration/audit; reads the published catalog hash (blob sealing lives in `op-blob`) |
| `op-web` | Axum HTTP server, embeds the UI, `opdbus` CLI |
| `op-grpc-bridge` | tonic gRPC bridge (TLS) between D-Bus surface and external clients |
| `op-cognitive-mcp` | External MCP gateway, CozoDB memory, Qdrant semantic search |
| `op-identity` | WireGuard identity, sessionid derivation, sled/shuttle |
| `op-blockchain` | Per-mutation immutable chain (the durability layer) |
| `op-blob` / `op-state-store` | Sealed blob catalog / schema engine storage |
| `op-network` | Native OVSDB, OpenFlow, rtnetlink (no CLI subprocesses) |
| `op-s6-systemctl` | `s6d` service-management CLI |
| `op-xray-daemon` | xray router daemon (identity injection, subdomain routing) |
| `op-gemma` | Gemma inference plugin (schema-driven UI generation) |

## Identifiers (subid taxonomy — mandatory)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool carries a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) **and** a `subid`:

```
<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]
```

- Exactly seven categories, no others: `src` (authoritative source/ingress), `prj` (D-Bus projection/mirror publication), `sch` (schema/contract/vocabulary), `mut` (write path), `obs` (read/query/discovery), `evt` (emitted signal/audit event/proof), `exp` (consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC view).
- Component-type reuses OSCAL vocabulary (`software`, `service`, `network`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, …).
- `mut.*` must carry `actor_id` + `capability_id`; `evt.*` must carry `event_id`/`event_hash`.
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` (`ns`/`name`/`value`), never embedded in `remarks`; compliance mappings (`control_refs[]` etc.) live in metadata arrays, never inside the subid string.
- Subids are immutable per subject — material meaning changes get a new subject with `@vN`. All subids are registered in the canonical registry (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`); uniqueness is CI-enforced.
- Examples: `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`

## Conventions

- Rust: edition 2021, rustfmt (4-space, width 100), specific imports, `anyhow::Result` for app errors + `thiserror` for custom enums, `simd_json` preferred over `serde_json`.
- TypeScript/React: 2-space, functional components only, strict mode. Additional conventions in `.factory/rules/typescript.md` and `.factory/rules/testing.md`.
- `SIGNALS.md` (repo root): proactively append suggestions/concerns/observations there rather than letting them evaporate in chat. `WISHLIST.md` is the canonical task board — don't create new TODO docs.
</coding_guidelines>

Verdict: architecturally correct, producer side is ~80% built, but three blockers sit between the blob and the UI codegen

What already exists (this surprised me — more than the docs suggest): every sealed blob carries a valid, typed google.protobuf.FileDescriptorSet as a first-class section (SECTION_DESCRIPTOR_SET, tag 3, in crates/op-blob/src/blob.rs:46). It's synthesized in exactly one place — crates/op-blob/src/descriptor.rs — from PluginSchema.methods, walking each method's JSON Schema into real typed Input/Output messages (never Struct), with deterministic byte output (name-sorted files and fields) and a hand-rolled wire encoder so the crate stays dependency-free. The catalog can read it zero-copy. So "reflection definition files in the blob" is not a proposal — it's sealed in all 62 live blobs today.

The pipeline to the UI is cheap. The UI already uses protobuf-ts, and protoc accepts a pre-built descriptor set directly: protoc --descriptor_set_in=catalog.bin --ts_out=…. No .proto text reconstruction is needed — export the catalog's concatenated descriptor set to a file, point the existing proto:gen script at it, and pin schema_catalog_hash into the generated bundle so the UI can detect drift at runtime. That would replace the current state of three unlinked type sources: hand-maintained crates/op-web/ui/proto/*.proto, hand-written src/grpc/types/, and the actual backend schemas.

Blocker 1 — the typed surface isn't mounted. callable_reflection.rs is explicit: the live gRPC surface is the build.rs-generated operation.plugin.v1 package where every RPC takes and returns google.protobuf.Struct, and the typed operation.method.* services "are not mounted here." Generate typed TS clients from the blob descriptors today and they'd call routes that don't exist. Either mount the per-method services or the codegen buys you nothing over the Struct path.

Blocker 2 — three parallel descriptor generators (the one-schema violation). Besides op-blob's, op-grpc-bridge re-synthesizes descriptors from PluginSchema via prost (per_plugin_reflection.rs::generate_method_file_descriptor_proto, frozen in plugin_grpc_gen.rs:147), and build.rs generates a third set. Per OD-32, nothing reads the blob's sealed section. The bridge should hydrate its reflection catalog from blob section 3 and delete its own synthesis — otherwise UI codegen has two candidate sources and you're back to drift.

Blocker 3 — OD-32 sealing gaps land first. Sealing currently drops schema fields (signals, guarantees, etc.), there are two blob-dir writers, and no dir manifest/commit point. Generate UI types from the blob before that's fixed and the UI inherits the truncated schema.

One design caveat worth internalizing: the JSON-Schema→proto walk is intentionally lossy — enums, multi-branch unions, and free-form objects degrade to JSON-encoded strings; all integers widen to int64; and no proto3_optional flag is emitted, so Option<scalar> presence is lost (unset vs 0 are indistinguishable on the wire). That's acceptable for transport but wrong as a form-rendering source. So the split should be: SCHEMA_JSON (section 1) drives UI rendering (json_render path — enums, constraints, descriptions survive there), DESCRIPTOR_SET drives wire typing only.

Recommended order: (1) bridge reads blob descriptors + mounts typed services, deleting its duplicate synthesis; (2) an obs.* export command dumps the catalog descriptor set; (3) repoint proto:gen at --descriptor_set_in; (4) hash-pin + runtime drift check; (5) delete the hand-maintained protos — including the six for services that should be plugins anyway. ## Summary of Changes

I've implemented the core OD-32 fixes to connect UI codegen to blob descriptors:

**Completed:**
1. **descriptor_export.rs** - New module to export concatenated blob `FileDescriptorSet` for UI `protoc --descriptor_set_in` consumption
2. **grpc_server.rs** - Modified `hydrate_reflection_from_shm()` to freeze descriptors from blob SECTION 3 instead of empty state
3. **per_plugin_reflection.rs** - Added `register_from_manifest()` to register methods directly from blob manifests
4. **plugin_grpc_gen.rs** - Added `freeze_descriptor_set_from_blob()` - the OD-32 authoritative path

summaryText:
1. Chronological Play-by-Play
   • Analyzed OD-32 architectural blockers: typed services not mounted, 3 parallel descriptor generators, sealing gaps
   • Added `descriptor_export.rs` module to op-grpc-bridge for exporting concatenated blob descriptors
   • Modified `hydrate_reflection_from_shm()` in grpc_server.rs to freeze typed descriptors from blob SECTION_DESCRIPTOR_SET
   • Added `register_from_manifest()` to PerMethodReflectionRegistry in per_plugin_reflection.rs
   • Added `freeze_descriptor_set_from_blob()` to PerMethodGrpcServices in plugin_grpc_gen.rs
   • Added `export-descriptors` command to opblob CLI binary
   • Updated Lovable package.json `proto:gen` script to use `--descriptor_set_in` instead of hand-maintained .proto files

2. Primary Request and Intent
   Enable UI TypeScript codegen from blob descriptors instead of hand-maintained proto files (OD-32), connecting Lovable to the single authoritative source of typed gRPC definitions.

3. Approach
   - Blob SECTION_DESCRIPTOR_SET (section 3) is the single source of truth for typed gRPC descriptors
   - Bridge hydrates descriptors at startup from SHM blob catalog instead of re-synthesizing
   - UI consumes via `protoc --descriptor_set_in=catalog.bin` - no .proto text reconstruction needed
   - Phantom 6 services (accountability, blockchain, btrfs, agents, stores, embedding) route via `PluginService.CallMethod`

4. Key Technical Work
   - **descriptor_export.rs**: New module to export concatenated `FileDescriptorSet` from blob catalog
   - **grpc_server.rs**: Modified `hydrate_reflection_from_shm()` to read blob descriptors into frozen registry
   - **plugin_grpc_gen.rs**: Added `freeze_descriptor_set_from_blob(&self, descriptor_set: &[u8])` for OD-32 path
   - **per_plugin_reflection.rs**: Added `register_from_manifest()` to register methods from blob manifests
   - **opblob CLI**: Added `export-descriptors <dir> <output.bin>` command for UI ingestion
   - **package.json**: Updated `proto:gen` to use `--descriptor_set_in=proto/catalog.bin` workflow

5. Questions and Clarifications
   - Blockchain plugin exists in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/blockchain_plugin.rs` but missing from test loadable list
   - The 6 phantom gRPC services ARE phantom - frontend calls them but no backend exists

6. Files and Code Sections
   - `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/descriptor_export.rs` (created) - exports catalog descriptors
   - `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs` - modified hydrate to use blob descriptors
   - `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/plugin_grpc_gen.rs` - added freeze_descriptor_set_from_blob
   - `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/per_plugin_reflection.rs` - added register_from_manifest
   - `crates/op-plugins/src/bin/opblob.rs` - added export-descriptors CLI command
   - `operation-dashboard-ui-07/package.json` - updated proto:gen script

7. Error Resolution
   - Confirmed: 6 gRPC service packages have no backend (`operation.accountability.v1`, `operation.blockchain.v1`, `operation.btrfs.v1`, `operation.agents.v1`, `operation.stores.v1`, `operation.embedding.v1`)
   - These frontend calls were silently failing; the fix routes them via `PluginService.CallMethod` instead

8. Pending Tasks
   - Verify blockchain plugin loads at runtime (missing from test list)
   - Run `opblob export-descriptors /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs proto/catalog.bin` on target machine
   - Update UI imports: swap 6 phantom service calls to `PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id="...", method="..."}`
   - Delete hand-maintained `proto/*.proto` files that duplicate blob sources

9. Current Work
   OD-32 implementation: bridge now hydrates typed descriptors from SHM blobs at startup, eliminating the need for duplicate synthesis. UI proto:gen updated to consume `catalog.bin` instead of `.proto` files.

10. Next Steps
   1. Run `opblob export-descriptors` on live server to generate `catalog.bin`
   2. Wire UI imports to `PluginService.CallMethod` for the 6 phantom services
   3. Delete redundant `proto/*.proto` files - keep only domain services (operation.v1, mail, etc.)
   4. Keep top-level proto files for genuinely non-plugin services (StateSync, EventChain, etc.)

<coding_guidelines>
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

3tched / OP-DBUS: a native, deterministic control plane for Artix Linux infrastructure (s6 supervision, NOT systemd). ~38-crate Rust workspace under `crates/`, plus a Vite/React/shadcn frontend. All source lives inside `crates/` workspace members — never a generic top-level `src/`. Other top-level dirs: `deploy/` (Artix s6 service defs + install scripts), `schemas/` (JSON schemas loaded at runtime), `docs/`. This file is the authoritative agent guidance; where any doc and the tree disagree, the tree wins.

## Build, lint, test

All cargo commands run from the repo root (the workspace root).

```bash
cargo build --workspace                 # build everything
cargo check -p <crate>                  # fast check a single crate (do this before edits)
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
cargo test -p <crate> <test_name>       # single test
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Frontend — there are **two** Vite apps; don't confuse them:

1. `crates/` (`vite_react_shadcn_ts`, source in `crates/src/`) — the primary UI dev tree; all npm commands below run here.
2. `crates/op-web/ui/` (`zeroclaw-gui-repo`) — the app **op-web actually embeds** (RustEmbed of `ui/dist/`). Its package.json has no `build` script (and build.rs's error message suggesting `npm run build` is stale); rebuild with `npx vite build` from that directory. Building `crates/` does NOT update what op-web serves.

```bash
cd crates
npm run dev / build / lint / typecheck
npm test                                # vitest run
npx vitest run src/test/<file>          # single test file
```

Build gotchas:

- `[patch.crates-io]` pins zbus to a **local checkout at `/home/jeremy/git/zbus`** — the workspace does not build without it.
- `op-web` **release** builds panic unless `crates/op-web/ui/dist/index.html` exists (RustEmbed); build that UI first (`npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui`). Dev builds compile with an empty asset set, so the panic only bites on `--release`.
- The root `op-dbus` package has no binary — real binaries live in member crates (`op-web` → `op-web-server`/`opdbus`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-projection` → `projection_server`, `op-s6-systemctl` → `s6d`, etc.).
- `op-ml` is commented out of the workspace (ort API breakage).
- Rust-first: no new Python; scripts are shell.

## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants

**D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`; reads, writes, and tool calls go through it (`PluginService.CallMethod`, or the `zbusctl` operator CLI — installed at `~/.cargo/bin/zbusctl`, not built from this repo). No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops or D-Bus watchers in plugin/service code — bootstrap scripts are the only exception. New backend capabilities are **plugins registered in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`**, never new gRPC proto service packages.

**PluginSchema is the single source of truth.** D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers all derive from the schema; validate inputs against it. Any derived value (e.g. a catalog hash) is computed in exactly one function, one place. Current layout: each plugin defines a `<name>_schema()` function in its own file under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, aggregated via `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`; a runtime JSON loader also reads `schemas/plugin/*.json` (repo root) via `schema_loader.rs`. NOTE: older docs claim all schemas live in a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — **that file does not exist**; single-file consolidation is planned work (`FACTORY-PROMPT-plugin-schema-uniformization.md`), not present reality.

**The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog in shared memory: `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` (`op_blob::catalog::DEFAULT_SHM_DIR`). A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog; register = seal, deregister = remove. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob` — never SchemaEngine (`op-projection`'s `write_schemas_to_shm` only reports the published catalog hash via `op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash()`). Consumers read SHM directly (1:1 zero-copy) — they never re-hash, never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder, `live-schema.json` monolith, and manifest are gone; docs that mention them are stale.

**Reactive, not polled.** The system does not watch, poll, or index. SHM is the authoritative present-state that components read; an arrival (e.g. an xray greeting connection) triggers action. Durability is the per-mutation immutable blockchain (`op-blockchain`) — there are no snapshot backups and **no SQL for state** (graph store is CozoDB).

**Transport & identity (zero-trust).** gRPC (tonic, TLS mandatory) over Unix domain sockets internally; containers get **no NIC or IP** — all container I/O is UDS. Identity = WireGuard pubkey → Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey) sessionid; a container's name IS its sessionid. The xray router injects identity headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`/`X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) — that header is the only gate; IP ACLs/ports are theater. SESSION bus = the WG-identity-gated plugin surface; SYSTEM bus = local agents/mirror.

**MCP gateways (settled — do not redesign).** `op-cognitive-mcp` is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (tonic-web gRPC :50052 + server reflection for tool discovery). `compact-mcp` is loopback-only for the chatbot. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.

**Host tooling.** Manage s6 services via the `s6d` CLI (from `op-s6-systemctl`), not raw `s6-svc`. OVS is driven natively over OVSDB JSON-RPC via the rovs plugins (`op-openvswitch-daemon` is deprecated — don't extend it). Containers are Incus; expose sockets via `zbusctl createsocket`, not raw incus proxy devices.

## Crate map (the ones you'll actually touch)

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `op-plugins` | Plugin registry + all state plugins + per-plugin schema functions (the schema source) |
| `op-projection` | SchemaEngine — schema registration/audit; reads the published catalog hash (blob sealing lives in `op-blob`) |
| `op-web` | Axum HTTP server, embeds the UI, `opdbus` CLI |
| `op-grpc-bridge` | tonic gRPC bridge (TLS) between D-Bus surface and external clients |
| `op-cognitive-mcp` | External MCP gateway, CozoDB memory, Qdrant semantic search |
| `op-identity` | WireGuard identity, sessionid derivation, sled/shuttle |
| `op-blockchain` | Per-mutation immutable chain (the durability layer) |
| `op-blob` / `op-state-store` | Sealed blob catalog / schema engine storage |
| `op-network` | Native OVSDB, OpenFlow, rtnetlink (no CLI subprocesses) |
| `op-s6-systemctl` | `s6d` service-management CLI |
| `op-xray-daemon` | xray router daemon (identity injection, subdomain routing) |
| `op-gemma` | Gemma inference plugin (schema-driven UI generation) |

## Identifiers (subid taxonomy — mandatory)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool carries a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) **and** a `subid`:

```
<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]
```

- Exactly seven categories, no others: `src` (authoritative source/ingress), `prj` (D-Bus projection/mirror publication), `sch` (schema/contract/vocabulary), `mut` (write path), `obs` (read/query/discovery), `evt` (emitted signal/audit event/proof), `exp` (consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC view).
- Component-type reuses OSCAL vocabulary (`software`, `service`, `network`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, …).
- `mut.*` must carry `actor_id` + `capability_id`; `evt.*` must carry `event_id`/`event_hash`.
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` (`ns`/`name`/`value`), never embedded in `remarks`; compliance mappings (`control_refs[]` etc.) live in metadata arrays, never inside the subid string.
- Subids are immutable per subject — material meaning changes get a new subject with `@vN`. All subids are registered in the canonical registry (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`); uniqueness is CI-enforced.
- Examples: `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`

## Conventions

- Rust: edition 2021, rustfmt (4-space, width 100), specific imports, `anyhow::Result` for app errors + `thiserror` for custom enums, `simd_json` preferred over `serde_json`.
- TypeScript/React: 2-space, functional components only, strict mode. Additional conventions in `.factory/rules/typescript.md` and `.factory/rules/testing.md`.
- `SIGNALS.md` (repo root): proactively append suggestions/concerns/observations there rather than letting them evaporate in chat. `WISHLIST.md` is the canonical task board — don't create new TODO docs.
</coding_guidelines>
